adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:151 — complete_offset() runs even when processing raises an exception, allowing failed results to be committed and permanently skipped.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in queue_consumer.py lines 127-151, the OrderedQueueWorker.run() method has a try/except/finally block where complete_offset() is called in the finally block (line 151). This means that even when an exception occurs during result_processor() execution (caught at line 143-145), the offset is still marked as complete. The OffsetTracker will then allow this offset to be committed, meaning the failed message will be permanently skipped and never reprocessed. This is a real bug - failed messages should not have their offsets committed as complete.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/result_consumer.py:254 — Closing a strategy permanently shuts down the shared factory-owned queue pool, so strategies recreated after rebalance cannot submit work and mark unprocessed messages complete after submission failures.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in result_consumer.py the `shutdown()` method at line 180-183 sets `self.queue_pool = None` after calling `queue_pool.shutdown()`. The `close()` method in SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy (line 254) calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`. The factory creates the queue_pool once in `__init__` (lines 128-133) and it's shared. When `create_with_partitions` is called (line 206-208), it creates a new SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy using the same `self.queue_pool`. If a strategy is closed (e.g., during rebalance), it shuts down the shared queue_pool. When a new strategy is created after rebalance, it would use the same (now shutdown) queue_pool from the factory. However, looking more carefully, the factory's `shutdown()` method sets `queue_pool = None`, but the strategy's `close()` only calls `queue_pool.shutdown()` without setting the factory's reference to None. This means the factory still holds a reference to a shutdown pool. On rebalance, `create_with_partitions` would return a new strategy with the shutdown pool, causing failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:187 — Unbounded queues and submission without backpressure allow queued messages and tracked offsets to grow without limit, eventually exhausting memory.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the Queue() objects created at line 187 in FixedQueuePool.__init__ are unbounded (no maxsize parameter), and the submit() method at line 203 uses put() without any backpressure mechanism. This means if producers submit faster than workers can process, memory usage will grow unboundedly. This is a legitimate architectural concern for a production consumer system, though not strictly a bug since the code functions as written. The diff shows queue.Queue() without maxsize, and put() without blocking/timeout considerations for backpressure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:237 — Shutdown sets worker exit flags before draining queued work, causing normal close()/join() to abandon pending processing.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in queue_consumer.py, the close() method at line 237 calls shutdown_event.set() and then queue_pool.shutdown(). The shutdown() method of FixedQueuePool (lines 230-242) sets worker.shutdown = True for all workers, then calls q.shutdown(immediate=False) on queues, then joins workers with timeout. The OrderedQueueWorker.run() method (lines 117-143) checks self.shutdown in its while loop condition. When shutdown=True is set, workers will exit their loop after completing current work item, but any items still in the queue won't be processed. The queue.shutdown(immediate=False) should allow draining, but setting worker.shutdown=True first means workers exit before fully draining. This is a real bug where pending work items could be abandoned during normal shutdown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:237 — Strategy closure stops the commit thread before workers finish, leaving final completed work uncommitted and causing replay on restart.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the close() method in SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy (lines 335-338), it first sets shutdown_event, then joins the commit_thread, then calls queue_pool.shutdown(). The commit_thread's _commit_loop (lines 275-293) checks shutdown_event.is_set() at the start of each iteration. When close() is called, the shutdown_event is set immediately, which causes the commit_loop to exit before it can commit any final offsets. Meanwhile, workers may still be processing items and completing offsets. The queue_pool.shutdown() is called after the commit_thread has already stopped, so any work completed by workers after the shutdown_event is set will never be committed. This is a real ordering bug - the commit thread should run until after workers are done, not before.
